implementation_notes: Ruby makes immutability a runtime property: Object#freeze prevents further in-place modification, frozen? reports it, and freeze applies to any object including arrays and hashes, while the frozen_string_literal magic comment freezes every string literal in a file and shareable_constant_value deep-freezes constants built from literals. Objects that are frozen and refer only to frozen objects are shareable between Ractors, which is how Ruby uses immutability for thread safety. The class itself is still hand-written - private readers, a constructor that assigns and then calls freeze, no writers - because nothing stops a caller from building an unfrozen instance, so the guarantee is per instance.
pitfalls: freeze is shallow and per object: a frozen Array or Hash does not freeze its elements, so a value holding a mutable child is not deeply immutable and is not Ractor-shareable.
Aliases created before the freeze stay visible, so build the whole object and freeze last; freezing an object that already leaked a mutable member only hides the leak.
A constant holding an unfrozen composite is deep-copied into each Ractor instead of being shared, and a non-shareable constant raises for a non-main Ractor.

variants.name: Data.define immutable value classes
variants.implementation_notes: Ruby 3.2 added Data, a minimal value-object class: Data.define(:time, :day) creates an immutable class whose instances are frozen as part of initialisation, expose readers but no writers, compare by value and support with(...) for a copy with changed members. It replaces the Struct-based value class that had to be frozen by hand and covers the common record case, while keeping the same caveat that a member referring to a mutable object is not itself made immutable.
variants.code_sketch:
Event = Data.define(:time, :day) do
  def same_day?(other) = day == other.day
end

e1 = Event.new(time: "09:00", day: "Mon")
e2 = e1.with(day: "Tue")     # a new frozen instance; e1 is unchanged
pitfalls: Data enforces no immutability on its members: the instance is frozen, but an Array or Hash member is still mutable through its reader and the instance then stops being Ractor-shareable.
Construction validates strictly - missing or unknown keywords raise - and with(...) reuses the same validation, so callers must pass every defined member.
